standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison of first Chern classes as cycles on integral schemes, and infinite sums of rational equivalences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-equal-c1-as-cycles (proof lines 5293 and 5297) and remark-infinite-sums-rational-equivalences (proof line 5298); the pullback diagram is described in remark-pullback-pairs (proof line 5277)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first identifies the two cycle classes in the two cases according to whether the component lies in the divisor, and the second extends the resulting equality from a single integral class to a general cycle.

core_obligations: Reduce to an integral class and split into two cases: for an integral closed subscheme of the source, either it is not contained in the base changed divisor, in which case both intersections with the divisors are computed as divisors of the restricted sections and the pushforward of one equals the other, or it is contained in the divisor, in which case the two caps with the first Chern classes correspond under pushforward (proof lines 5283-5297).
Extend to general cycles by the statement on infinite sums (proof lines 5298-5299).
proof_roadmap: Integral class and the two cases (proof lines 5283-5297).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the Gysin map commutes with the proper pushforward of the ambient scheme, on the level of cycles (statement lines 5263-5281, tag 02TN-adjacent). The proof reduces to an integral class and distinguishes whether it is contained in the base changed divisor, using the comparison of first Chern classes as cycles in both cases, and then extends the equality to general cycles by the infinite sums statement. The two-case analysis is the substance, so the claim is H2.
